items.title: Using the stack-frame tests as design-enforcement tool.
items.box:
Using the stack-frame tests as design-enforcement tool.

WHAT EXISTS (paths under spirit/test/)
- tools/wirePaths.js records, during the suites it drives, every call stack inside our own code that reaches a bottom, and ranks the paths. A stack sees where code arrives, not what it resembles, so it finds a second route to the same place even when no name or text is shared.
- Its bottoms: wire (the network), fs-write, crypto, child-process, and two components, presenceNode and postQueue.
- oneDoorStacks.js (goal/G19.14) is the enforcing suite: one test per bottom that names a door. It runs that row's suites and fails on any stack with a production frame (spirit/run/) and no frame in the door. Stacks with no production frame are a suite unit-testing the component and are not counted. A run that never reaches the component fails.
- Two doors are enforced today: nobody but peerPost reaches presenceNode, and nobody but peerPost reaches postQueue.
- oneDoorStacks.js is part of run all: runAll.js and deskVerify's full run both take every suite in spirit/test.

HOW IT ENFORCES A DESIGN
- A design rule of the form "only this door may reach that component" becomes one row: the door, the component, and the suites that drive it.
- The wire, fs-write, crypto and child-process bottoms are measured but have no door yet; each ruling such as "only X writes to disk" costs one row.

ITS LIMIT
- It sees only the paths the driven suites walk: a row is as good as its suites, and a path no suite exercises stays invisible.

2. It is part of run all: runAll.js lists it, and so does deskVerify's full run, since both take every suite in spirit/test. It is not stand-alone.

now we create a new item for another stack-path we want to control, inside peerPost

suggestions?

Of peerPost's components, two are worth a row next:
1. sseClient, the stream to a relay: only peerPost and presenceNode (itself a peerPost component) use it today, so the row locks in a state that is already clean. The cheapest.
2. seal, the one sealing implementation: on the node side only peerPost uses it; hub, relay and relayServer use it on the relay side, so that row needs one door per side. The most valuable: a second sealing path is how associated data gets dropped.
I'd take sseClient first; say which and I propose the item.
can you name one you know would fail?

Yes: "nobody but peerPost talks to a relay". The desk's offboard.js fetches the relay's key straight from the relay over plain fetch (process/js/desk/offboard.js line 78), so a wire row with peerPost as its door fails on it, as long as a driven suite runs offboard.
A softer one: relayKeys, the relay table, is read outside peerPost by answerRelay, ownerBadge and server.js; that fails too, but reading a table may be allowed by design.
I'd take the offboard one: it is a real second road to a relay.
make THAT one an item.

items.title: Nobody but peerPost talks to a relay
items.box:
Nobody but peerPost talks to a relay.

DECIDED (Andy, 2026-10-13)
- The purpose of this item is to add one row to the stack-frame test (oneDoorStacks.js, through tools/wirePaths.js): every request our production code sends to a relay must have peerPost on its stack. That is all it does.
- Its red goes into another suite, stackFrameTestItems.js in spirit/test, which asserts that this row exists in the stack-frame test; it is red until the row is added and green after.
- The row is committed failing on purpose: oneDoorStacks and goal/G22.1 are meant to fail, so that a pattern can be developed that guides the fixes for this kind of failure. The fixes come in later items, not in this one.

FOUND (b29bf3ac, 2026-10-13; paths under spirit/run/)
- Relay traffic is told apart by path: every request under /api/relay/, which a relay answers and a node never does, so a process asking its own node is not counted even when a lab relay also listens on loopback.
- The probe also watches global fetch, which never passes through http.request.
- The row is driven by agentOnboard.js (the only suite that runs offboard) and serverSurface.js.
- The row finds 7 paths to a relay without peerPost: process/js/desk/offboard.js line 78 (fetch of the relay key); and through js/relayRequest.js, from js/hub.js (key at 300 and 2651, claim at 1084), js/ownerBadge.js 369 (directly and via hub 2784), and js/answerRelay.js 35 (key).
